newsitem.title: USA: Senate resolution challenges mammogram advice.
newsitem.headline: Senate resolution challenges mammogram advice.

text.p: The Senate Tuesday unanimously passed a nonbinding resolution urging the National Cancer Institute to consider recommending mammograms for women in their 40s and to do more research on the value of the breast cancer screening x-rays.

The "Sense of the Senate" resolution, sponsored by Maine Republican Olympia Snowe and passed by a 98-0 vote, suggested that in the meantime women consider the advice of health groups other than the National Cancer Institute "until there is more definite data."
The American Cancer Society, for instance, recommends routine screening for women in their 40s.
Nobody doubts the benefit of mammograms for women aged 50-69 but an emotional controversy has raged for several years about whether women aged 40-49 should have the breast cancer screening.

An advisory committee to the cancer institute in late January met to try to settle the debate, but ended up provoking even more confusion by saying women and their doctors should make up their own minds. The Senate resolution urged that that recommendation be reconsidered.
The National Cancer Institute used to recommend screening for women in their 40s, but changed course in 1993 after some studies suggested it may not save many lives.

Opponents of routine screening for that age group also cite the limitations of mammograms in younger women that lead to a high number of false positives that require surgical biopsies and huge stress.

National Cancer Institute director Dr. Richard Klausner, who took the unusual step of publicly differing with the advisory panel, is among the witnesses scheduled to appear before a Senate Appropriations subcommittee Wednesday on the issue.
